subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.11 published dist missing reentrancy guard - reply session initialization conflicted

question: Should maintainers publish a corrected stable package for the 2026.6.11 reply-session dist/source divergence now, or wait for the next scheduled release with an explicit affected-version notice?
rationale: The source fix is present on main, but deciding whether to republish or hotfix a stable npm artifact and how to communicate affected versions is a release ownership decision, not a source-only repair decision.

options.title: Publish corrected stable
options.body: Cut a stable hotfix or next patch release from current main with package-parity proof for the reentrant store-writer path.

options.title: Document affected release
options.body: Leave 2026.6.11 as the latest stable temporarily but clearly mark it affected and point users to beta, main build, or rollback guidance.

options.title: Wait for scheduled release
options.body: Keep this issue open until the next planned release ships and then close with the release tag and validation evidence.

recommendation.title: Publish corrected stable
recommendation.body: Cut a stable hotfix or next patch release from current main with package-parity proof for the reentrant store-writer path.

likelyOwner.reason: They already provided the issue's source-vs-release distinction and are the clearest routing candidate in the discussion for the release decision.
